headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar, though the gap is narrower than in round 1. The register is fixed: the sad lonely machine is mostly gone, and Nav now assumes the star will comply ('You cannot change it while moving', 'Some of them damp'). Cover the names and the road nouns, though, and the sentence shape is still the house shape: two or three flat declaratives with no contractions and the payoff in the last clause. Crumb ('Notice: ... This has never happened.') and Maximilian (no contractions, 'I shall have that removed') write the same way. Of Nav's best 12, only 'Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop.' is built on the satnav's own grammar, a second-person command with a distance. The rest are anecdotes and reports, and only the vocabulary (route, destination, toll) marks them as Nav. Vera is identified by syntax alone: the 'Right?' tag that assumes you agree, the fake-out repetition ('my career... my career on'), the complaint dressed as a boast, the SUCH in caps.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours. Taken line for line, Nav's best 12 are tighter than Vera's: each has a real turn, specific nouns (bollard, ambulances, 'no results found', 'while moving') and the payoff last. Vera's #45 runs past its own joke and #51 is a lecture. The win stops at the top 12. Below it, the bank still adds codas after the joke has landed ('Then continue straight.', 'Indicate left.', 'Tell nobody.', 'Respectfully.', 'Or do not.', 'Mostly.', 'This time.', 'We have that in common.'), which breaks Nav's own tic 'nothing after it'. Triple repetition also keeps standing in for a turn.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. Ours has five or six lines you would clip ('Then they phone me from a field.', 'a full stop', 'So is a bollard', 'looks buoyant', 'Some of them damp'). Most of them clip as a good satnav joke. Vera's clip as a person: 'cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?' shows her whole moral universe in one breath, and nothing of Nav's does that yet. The nearest is 'You cannot change it while moving'.

templates: Rival deleted from the map: the rival becomes an 'alternative route', a 'road closure', or something removed or rerouted to a car park. There are 8 lines of this, two of them closing on the same 'Nobody presses / Nobody checks those'. It replaced round 1's 'rival is a road that goes nowhere' template, the right direction (Nav now acts rather than observes), but it is still one joke in eight places.

Asked for a route, sent somewhere absurd, still there: bathroom via the motorway, Quill to a cobbled car park, Brock to a lighthouse, the concierge's guests 'still out there', plus car wash, marathon, ditch, ferry and Wales. This is persona move three, and the ending 'He has not come down' / 'still out there' / 'He has proposed to it' runs on the same rails every time.

biggestGap: Only the road nouns mark Nav now. The satnav's own grammar, a second-person command with a distance that the listener is assumed to obey ('Sir Quill, in two hundred feet, a full stop.'), carries fewer than ten of 112 lines; the rest are past-tense anecdotes and flat reports in the house shape that Crumb and Maximilian share. In the next pass, rewrite the misrouting anecdotes and rival deletions as live instructions to whoever is in the room, ending on the command (not 'Brock asked for the gym. I gave him a lighthouse.' but 'Brock, in two hundred feet, a lighthouse. Climb. Keep climbing.'), so that with every noun covered the imperative-plus-distance shape alone says Nav, the way 'Right?' alone says Vera.

notes: Sources: refs/writing/monster-prom-lines.md was present and read in full; refs/writing/charm-notes.md was present and skimmed. Bank: 112 lines, counted by script; none is over its word limit (the three-words twist cap of 3 comes from decks.json). Progress since round 1 is real. The sad-arrival and 'recalculating means I am sad' lines are gone, the {played}/{losses} digit placeholders are gone, the darling/you'll-be-mine rhyme is gone, and the persona's status move now drives most lines ('You cannot change it while moving', 'Strangers will drive there by accident', 'Help is not coming'). Generic share is down from 48% to 43%. Construction at the top of the bank now beats the bar. What keeps the bar ahead: the voice is identified by vocabulary rather than syntax, and the bank found new templates (rival deleted from the map, triple repetition) to replace the old ones. Opener 1 is the CAST.md sample line copied verbatim, then re-used in oneOnOne.any. Collisions with the cast: Nav's Tilly jab ('on this sentence for six minutes') is the same joke as Pixel's cringe reaction to Nav, and the 'calm' praise is shared by three stars. Crumb's bank (suitors/frost.json) is still written as a fridge, against the recast note. That is not Nav's problem, but it is why Nav and Crumb read alike: both are flat appliance deadpan. Vera stays the bar over Calculester because Calculester is the earnest anxious learner, the register Nav has rightly left behind.
